terms.definition: A manufacturing process that builds objects layer by layer directly from digital models, in contrast to subtractive methods that remove material.
A common term for additive manufacturing, in which successive layers of material are deposited or fused to create a three-dimensional object.
The fast fabrication of a physical part or model from a digital design, used to validate concepts and iterate quickly.
A prototype made with production-representative materials so it can be tested under real-world mechanical and environmental conditions.
The practice of designing parts specifically to take advantage of additive manufacturing capabilities and constraints.
Production of small to medium quantities of parts, often without dedicated tooling, suited to short runs and bridge production.
The thickness of each individual layer deposited during printing, which influences surface finish, detail, and build time.
The maximum three-dimensional space in which a printer can produce a part, defining the largest object it can create in one build.
Steps performed after printing, such as support removal, curing, sanding, or finishing, to achieve the desired final part quality.
Temporary printed structures that hold up overhanging features during a build and are removed during post-processing.
The allowable deviation from a specified dimension, indicating how precisely a manufactured part matches its design.
The use of digital design and data-driven workflows to plan, produce, and optimize physical parts, including additive processes.
